title: Trump reposts Senator-elect El-Sayed's "TrumpCare" card for Medicare for All, with no comment
dek: A Democrat's offer to put the president's name on universal health coverage got a repost from the president. The White House then rejected the idea.
what: On Saturday, 21 November 2026, President Trump reposted on Truth Social a post by Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic senator-elect from Michigan. Fox 2 Detroit reports that the repost had no caption from Trump.

El-Sayed's post showed a mock gold "TrumpCare" insurance card with Medicare for All on it. His caption, as reported, read: "Donald, this is on the table. Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave." Fox 2 Detroit dates the first version of the pitch to 12 November.
After the repost, El-Sayed posted: "Let's get to work, then. Ready when you are."
A White House spokeswoman, Allison Schuster, told Fox News Digital the plan should be called "Medicare for None" and called it a "government takeover of healthcare."
A repost is not an endorsement. I found no statement of Trump's own about the plan, and no bill text.
why: One image drew two readings. Supporters of Medicare for All see an opening. Some conservative outlets, such as RedState, describe the repost as Trump trolling El-Sayed. Both readings rest on a post with no words.
next: Whether Trump says anything himself, or El-Sayed files a bill.
